History_Part_1: had established Maharashtra State Technical Education Examination Board (MSBTEE) in 1956 under Directorate of Technical Education. Due to the exponential growth of technical and vocational education, the Government of Maharashtra bifurcated Directorate of Technical Education and established the Directorate of Vocational Education and Training in 1986. Subsequently, the Maharashtra State Technical Education Examination Board (MSBTEE) was bifurcated, and the Maharashtra State Vocational Education Examination Board (MSBVEE) was established on 23.01.1986 by Government Resolution.
History_Part_2: Maharashtra State Vocational Education Examination Board (MSBVEE) was renamed and established as Maharashtra State Board of Skill, Vocational Education and Training. It regulates matters related to Skill, Vocational Education, and Training as per the National Skill Qualification Framework and other skills courses in Maharashtra, as per the Maharashtra State Board of Skill, Vocational Education and Training Act, 2021 (Mah. Act No. IX of 2022), which came into force on 26.01.2022.
Functions_Intro: The functions of the Board are broadly classified as follows:
MSCVT_Heading: Maharashtra State Council of Vocational Training (MSCVT)
MSCVT_Description: MSCVT was established by the Education and Employment Department, Government of Maharashtra, on 25.09.1984. MSCVT was subsequently registered under the Society Registration Act, 1860, on 29.03.2017, as per the directives of the Directorate General of Training, Government of India. Since the functions of MSCVT and the Board overlapped, MSCVT has been merged into the Board, and all activities of MSCVT and affiliated institutes have been transferred to the Board on 16.02.2022.
Board_Courses_Description: The Board offers varied duration Certificate Courses, 2-year Diploma Courses, and 1-year Advanced Diploma Courses through 1265 affiliated institutes. In addition to its own courses, the Board has adopted courses designed by Sector Skill Councils. Both the number of courses and institutes are growing exponentially.
Training_Programs_Description: All training programs under the Board are conducted on a permanent self-financed basis. The Maharashtra State Skill Development Society (MSSDS) assigns batches for conducting training programs in NSQF courses in over 6500 institutes. The MSSDS manages the scheme and training, but the assessment of trainees at the end of training is conducted by the Board, with certificates issued to qualifying trainees.
Green_Channel_Description: As per Government letter dated 01.02.2022, skill training institutes established by reputed Industrial Establishments, Public Universities, nationally renowned Institutes (IIT/IIM), and institutes under International Agreements are approved through the Green Channel process. The Board has approved institutes from various sectors such as the Agricultural Science Center, Women Economic Development Corporation, Khadi and Cottage Industries Center, Industrial Establishments, Colleges, Hospitals, Non-Government Social Organizations, etc.
Salient_Feature_1: Board courses are divided into 38 different sectors. The courses are designed to give hands-on experience in the respective skill sets, with 70-80% of the course being practical-based.
Salient_Feature_2: Two-year duration courses are given equivalency to 12th Standard of Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary School Examination, Pune (Govt. Resolution dated 28.09.2012).
Salient_Feature_3: One- and two-year courses are recognized as an alternative qualification to the respective ITI trades for job purposes by industries (Govt. Resolution dated 28.09.2012).
Salient_Feature_4: The Board grants certificates under the name "Diploma Course" to the full-time 2-year duration courses with an entry qualification of 10th standard (Govt. Resolution dated 21.01.2013).
Salient_Feature_5: Computer group courses are recognized as a Computer Qualification for State Government service (Govt. Resolution dated 04.02.2013).
Salient_Feature_6: Architectural Draftsman and Construction Supervisor courses are approved as equivalent to "Civil Engineering Assistant" in Public Works Department (Govt. Resolution dated 11.03.2008).
Salient_Feature_7: Construction Supervisor courses are approved for appointment to the post of Junior Engineering Assistant at Zilla Parishad by nomination (Govt. Resolution dated 26.11.1997).
Salient_Feature_8: 123 Courses are notified under the Apprenticeship Training Scheme by the Government of India (Gazette Notification dated 07.09.2017).
Salient_Feature_9: Candidates passing the "Boiler Attendant" course with 1 year of experience are eligible for endorsement as Fireman or Assistant Operator on steam boilers (Govt. Gazette dated 09.05.2012).
Salient_Feature_10: Shorthand and Typing certificates are accepted for posts of Teachers, Instructors, and Stenographers in Government and Semi-Government Services (Govt. Resolution dated 02.09.1994).
Salient_Feature_11: Candidates who have completed 2-year Diploma courses are qualified for direct second-year admission to Post SSC Diploma courses of MSBTE.
Salient_Feature_12: Candidates completing 2-year Diploma courses are eligible for first-year admission to Post HSC Diploma courses of MSBTE.
Salient_Feature_13: Candidates completing training in specific Diploma courses are qualified for admission to B.Voc. courses at Tata Institute of Social Sciences.
Salient_Feature_14: Candidates with relevant experience can appear for direct examination for selected courses (Direct Admission to Examination).
Salient_Feature_15: Candidates are eligible for a 66.67% travel fare concession for travel by Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation buses.
Assessment_1: Assessment is done at the end of training for certificate courses and annually for Diploma and Advance Diploma courses.
Assessment_2: The assessment includes both formative and summative evaluations of trainee performance.
Assessment_3: Board conducts assessments for trainees under District, State, and Central schemes along with CSR-funded and self-funded programs.
Assessment_4: Board conducts practical examinations for technical subjects on behalf of Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary School Examination, Pune.
Assessment_5: Assessment statements are issued to trainees, and certificates are given to those who qualify.
Course_Duration_Highlight: Course Duration: 30 hours to 2 years (Diploma and Advance Diploma are full-time; Certificate courses are part-time)
Apprenticeship_Highlight: Apprenticeship: 123 courses are under the Apprenticeship Training Scheme by the Government of India (Gazette Notification dated 07.09.2017).
Vision Description: To be a leading organization to strengthen Skills, Vocational Education and Training system by making the youth of Maharashtra globally employable as per the demand of the industry and society at large.
Mission Description: To build the capacity of Vocational Education and Training, Skill and Entrepreneurship training institutions for making the youth of Maharashtra globally employable as per the need of the current and future market.
Objective_1: Developing competent, skilled and capable youth imbued with skills, learning and the spirit of entrepreneurship.
Objective_2: Promoting vocational education at secondary and higher secondary education.
Objective_3: Creating dedicated skill eco-systems by strengthening institute-industry interactions.
Objective_4: Undertaking labor market study at a regular interval.
Objective_5: Upgrading the existing skillset of the teachers.
Objective_6: Extending opportunities of training to all sections of society.
Objective_8: Promoting inclusive growth to enhance livelihood of beneficiaries.
Goal_1: To build/create over 5 Lakh Capacity of Employable Youth per year by 2030.
Goal_2: Introducing Industry 4.0 and future skill courses covering all sectors.
Goal_3: To provide adequate training in market-relevant skills by giving affiliation to 10,000 institutes by 2030.

Quote_1: Our department is committed to ensuring every youth in the state gets world-class skill training and employment opportunities.
Quote_2: Skill development of the new generation is a national need and is the foundation of Aatmanirbhar Bharat
Quote_3: Today, as we transform from an industrial powerhouse to a skill capital, our youth will lead India's journey toward becoming the global talent hub.
Short_Content: In today's rapidly evolving industrial landscape, technical competency and adaptability have become crucial for sustainable employment and career growth. Industrial Training Institutes (ITI) serve as vital bridges between theoretical education and practical industry requirements, offering students the opportunity to develop job-ready skills that align with market demands.
Section_1_Content: Short-term skill courses represent focused, intensive training programs designed to equip students with specific competencies in minimal time. These courses offer several key advantages:
Section_2_Content: Unlike traditional long-term programs, short-term courses are designed to address current industry needs and emerging technologies. They provide students with skills that are directly applicable in today's job market.
Section_3_Content: Employers increasingly value candidates with specialized skills and practical experience. Short-term courses help students stand out in competitive job markets by demonstrating their commitment to continuous learning and professional development.
Section_4_Content: These courses accommodate various schedules and backgrounds, making skill development accessible to working professionals, recent graduates, and career changers alike.
Section_5_Content: ITI institutions are uniquely positioned to deliver effective short-term skill training due to their industry connections, practical training facilities, and experienced instructors. When enrolling in ITI short-term courses, students benefit from:
Benefit_1: Industry-Standard Equipment: Access to modern machinery and tools used in actual work environments
Benefit_2: Experienced Faculty: Instructors with real-world industry experience who understand current market requirements
Benefit_3: Industry Partnerships: Direct connections with employers and potential job placement opportunities
Benefit_4: Certification Value: Recognized credentials that carry weight with employers across various industries
Section_6_Title: The Strategic Advantage of Advanced Courses During Regular Training
Section_6_Content: Pursuing advanced short-term skill courses while completing regular ITI training creates a powerful synergy that significantly enhances career prospects. This dual approach offers several strategic benefits:
Section_7_Content: While regular training provides foundational knowledge, advanced courses add specialized expertise that sets students apart from their peers. This combination creates well-rounded professionals with both breadth and depth of knowledge.
Section_8_Content: In today's job market, having additional certifications and specialized skills often determines who gets selected for premium positions. Students who invest in advanced training during their regular course demonstrate initiative and commitment to excellence.
Section_9_Content: Employers are willing to offer better compensation packages to candidates with advanced skills and multiple certifications. The additional investment in training often pays for itself through higher initial salaries and faster career progression.
Section_10_Content: Technology and industry practices evolve rapidly. Students who develop the habit of continuous learning during their foundational training are better prepared to adapt to future changes and remain relevant throughout their careers.
Section_11_Content: Advanced courses often bring together motivated individuals from various backgrounds, creating valuable professional networks that can benefit students throughout their careers.
Section_12_Content: Advanced skills learned through additional courses can be integrated into regular training projects, creating more impressive portfolios and practical experience that employers value.
Section_13_Content: To fully leverage the opportunities available at ITI, students should approach their education strategically. This means viewing regular training as the foundation and using advanced short-term courses to build specialized expertise on top of that foundation. The combination creates a powerful skill set that addresses both current industry needs and future opportunities.
Section_14_Content: Students who embrace this approach often find themselves with multiple career paths available upon completion of their training. They become candidates not just for entry-level positions, but for roles requiring specialized knowledge and advanced technical competencies.

act2013.title: The Maharashtra Unauthorized Institutions and Unauthorized Courses of Study in Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Sciences, Health Sciences, Higher, Technical and Vocational Education (Prohibition) Act, 2013 - Maharashtra Act No. XX OF 2013
act2013.point1: No person shall establish or cause to be established or conduct an Educational Institution, without prior approval of the appropriate authority.
act2013.point2: No person or an Educational Institution shall introduce or cause to be introduced or conduct a programme or course of study in Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Sciences, Health Sciences, Higher Education, Technical Education or Vocational Education without prior approval of the appropriate authority.
act2013.point3: No person or any Educational Institution shall publish or cause to be published, or arrange or take part in the publication or exhibition of any advertisement relating to such Educational Institution or programmes or courses of study conducted in such Educational Institution or centre which he knows or believes to be not true, intending thereby to cause or knowing it to be likely to make another person believe that the said Educational Institution or programme or course of study is approved by the appropriate authority.
act2013.moreDetails: For more details, refer copy of the Act.

rules2024.title: Maharashtra Unauthorized Institutions and Unauthorized Courses of Study in Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Sciences, Health Sciences, Higher, Technical and Vocational Education (Complaints, Appeals and Remedial Measures) Rules, 2024
rules2024.point1: In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 18 read with sub-sections (5) and (6) of section 6, sub-section (2) of section 8 and clause (vii) of section 12 of the Maharashtra Unauthorized Institutions and Unauthorized Courses of Study in Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Sciences, Health Sciences, Higher, Technical and Vocational Education (Prohibition) Act, 2013 (Mah. XX of 2013) and of all other powers enabling it in that behalf, the Government of Maharashtra, hereby makes Maharashtra Unauthorized Institutions and Unauthorized Courses of Study in Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Sciences, Health Sciences, Higher, Technical and Vocational Education (Complaints, Appeals and Remedial Measures) Rules, 2024.
rules2024.point2: These rules came into force from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette i.e. 8th October, 2024.
rules2024.moreDetails: For more details, refer copy of the Rules.

dvet.title: Directorate of Vocational Education and Training
dvet.para1: Directorate of Vocational Education and Training (DVET) established in 1984 is entrusted with the administrative responsibilities in respect of Craftsman Training Scheme (Industrial Training Institutes - ITI), Apprentice Training Scheme, Pre SSC Vocational Education, +2 Level Vocational Education (HSC Vocational) and +2 Level Bifocal Vocational Education.
dvet.para2: Industrial Training Institute (ITI) are granted affiliation by Directorate General of Training, New Delhi based on Letter of Intent (LoI) issued by Government of Maharashtra. Application for Letter of Intent (LoI) are accepted and processed by DVET. Exams are conducted and certificates are issued to successful candidates by Directorate General of Training, New Delhi through DVET.
dvet.para3: Application for establishing institute for Pre SSC Vocational Education, +2 Level Vocational Education (HSC Vocational) and +2 Level Bifocal Vocational Education are also accepted and processed by Directorate of Vocational Education and Training. Exams are conducted and certificates are issued by Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education.

act2021.title: Maharashtra State Board of Skill, Vocational Education and Training Act, 2021 - Maharashtra Act No. IX of 2022
act2021.para1: Maharashtra State Vocational Education Examination Board (MSBVEE) established in 1986 is now renamed and reconstituted as Maharashtra State Board of Skill, Vocational Education and Training (Board) to regulate matters pertaining to Skill, Vocational Education and Training and Entrepreneurship Education as per the National Skill Qualification Framework and other Skills Courses in the State of Maharashtra and for other matters vide Maharashtra State Board of Skill, Vocational Education and Training Act, 2021 (Mah. Act No. IX of 2022) dated 20.01.2022 which came into force on 26.01.2022.
act2021.para2: Maharashtra State Board of Skill, Vocational Education and Training has been entrusted with responsibility design and approve courses, affiliation of training institutes, assessment and certification of Certificate, Diploma and Advance Diploma level Vocational Education and Training, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Education courses.
act2021.para3: Institutes imparting training in Certificate, Diploma and Advance Diploma level Vocational Education and Training, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Education courses should seek affiliation from Maharashtra State Board of Skill, Vocational Education and Training.

competentAuthority.title: Competent Authority and Appellate Authority for Vocational Education
competentAuthority.para1: Director, Directorate of Vocational Education and Training is designated as Competent Authority for Vocational Education.
competentAuthority.para2: Joint/ Deputy Secretary-in-Charge of Vocational Education and Training, Government of Maharashtra, Mantralaya, Mumbai is designated as Appellate Authority for Vocational Education.

factFinding.title: Fact Finding Committee constituted by Competent Authority
factFinding.para1: Director, Directorate of Vocational Education and Training who is designated as Competent Authority has constituted Fact Finding Committee (FCC) as per provision at rule 5 of Maharashtra Unauthorized Institutions and Unauthorized Courses of Study in Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Sciences, Health Sciences, Higher, Technical and Vocational Education (Complaints, Appeals and Remedial Measures) Rules, 2024.
factFinding.para2: The Fact Finding Committee (FCC) shall make an inquiry as per provisions of the said rules whether the Institute is established or any programme or course of study is introduced or conducted in contravention of any of the provisions of the Act. After completing the inquiry, the Fact Finding Committee (FCC) shall submit its report to the Competent Authority within the given time limit.
